speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Lyme Arthritis). The history of recent camping in Minnesota, a self-resolving monoarticular knee pain (suggestive of early disseminated Lyme arthritis), and the current presentation of oligoarthritis (wrist), fever, and chills are highly characteristic of Lyme carditis/arthritis or early disseminated infection, despite the normal ANA and RPR results.
